clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12376, whose subject line describes increasing membership on the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving. The single sentence amends the second sentence of section 1 of Executive Order 12358 of April 14, 1982 so that the Commission is composed of no more than 28 members appointed by the President (an increase of two). The amendment became part of the text of the parent order; the table of Executive Order 12553 lists this order by number and subject, so the revocation reaches it expressly, and no source shows the amendment being undone earlier. Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 amended only section 4(b) of the parent order (the Commission’s termination date), not the membership sentence; it is a source note and not an end. The parent Commission's own termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 (48 FR 15117) amended section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12358, as amended, to provide that the Commission shall terminate on December 31, 1983, and no held instrument extends it, so the Commission, and with it the membership ceiling this order set, had no operation after December 31, 1983 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading). That instrument does not name Executive Order 12376, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is not an end; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. No earlier express end was found.
